articles.title: Pedro Martínez: un récord de 1.112 partidos en ACB y un frondoso árbol genealógico
articles.standfirst: Este domingo se convierte en el entrenador con más encuentros en la historia de la competición superando a Aíto García Reneses
articles.summary: Este domingo se convierte en el entrenador con más encuentros en la historia de la competición superando a Aíto García Reneses
articles.body: Después de dos duras derrotas, no parece el mejor momento para celebrar, pero este domingo, cuando arranque el Real Madrid-Asisa Joventut, nadie habrá dirigido más encuentros en la ACB que Pedro Martínez. El técnico blanco alcanzará los 1.112, superando a uno de sus referentes, Aíto García Reneses, aunque él llegó a los 1.359 contando los de Liga Nacional. El destino ha querido que el récord caiga ante la Penya, el equipo en el que Martínez se estrenó el 8 de marzo de 1990 ganando al CAI Zaragoza por 100-84. “Fue mi primer equipo y es como la primera novia, que tienes un recuerdo con más cariño porque en los inicios todo lo vives con más intensidad emocional”, contaba el técnico en palabras a la web de la ACB. Para demostrar lo que ha cambiado el baloncesto, señalar que entonces se jugaban dos periodos en lugar de cuatro cuartos, el triple estaba aún en 6,25 metros y se tiraban muchos menos —aquel día los verdinegros lanzaron sólo nueve y metieron cinco—, las plantillas eran cortas —saltaron a la pista ocho jugadores— y las rotaciones casi no existían —cuatro de ellos llegaron a 34 minutos—. Una muestra de la capacidad de adaptación de Martínez al paso del tiempo y a los distintos estilos de juego. En su larguísima trayectoria en los banquillos, el técnico ha hecho varias vueltas a España. Acumula 12 equipos ACB, compartiendo récord con su amigo Luis Casimiro, el segundo entrenador con más partidos en activo (824). En la lista de Martínez están el mencionado Joventut, Manresa en varias ocasiones, Salamanca, Granada, Ourense, Granca también repitiendo, Baskonia en dos etapas, Estudiantes, Akasvayu Girona, Cajasol, Valencia con otros dos periodos y, finalmente, Real Madrid. Entre todos esos clubes, 599 victorias, a una de otra cifra redonda. En lo más alto de su palmarés, las dos Ligas conquistadas con el Valencia Basket (2017 y la temporada pasada). También dos Supercopas Endesa (Baskonia 2005 y con el equipo taronja 2025). A nivel europeo, la Korac que le ganó nada más debutar en 1990 al Scavolini de un también jovencísimo Sergio Scariolo. Sin embargo, el partido del que mejor recuerdo guarda Martínez no dio un título, sino una permanencia. La del Manresa, que en 2015 se salvó ganando al Madrid en el Palacio en la última jornada. “Ese siempre quedará para mi historia personal”, reconoce. A lo largo de su carrera, ha dirigido a un total de 377 jugadores. Entre ellos, algunos de los más longevos de la historia de la ACB: Rafa Jofresa (2º), Marcelinho Huertas (3°), Nacho Azofra (5°), Sergio Llull (6°), Albert Oliver (9°) y Fran Vázquez (10°). Con el que más ha coincidido, Tomás Bellas. En sus discípulos ha dejado huella. Muchos pasaron al banquillo al acabar sus carreras. Joan Peñarroya, Pablo Prigioni, Pedro Rivero, su actual ayudante Salva Camps... Incluso tres han alcanzado la NBA como primeros entrenadores: Kenny Atkinson (Cavaliers), que recientemente reconocía que le copiaba algunas jugadas, Ime Udoka (Rockets) y Tiago Splitter (Bulls). Como sucede con Gregg Popovich en la NBA, el árbol genealógico de entrenadores que fueron sus ayudantes tiene muchas ramas. Martínez ha tenido ilustres colaboradores como Casimiro, Jaume Ponsarnau, Diego Ocampo, Xavi Albert, Salva Maldonado, Víctor García, Mariano de Pablos, Carles Marco, Israel González, Himar Ojeda, actual director deportivo de ALBA Berlín, y Xevi Pujol, que ocupa el mismo cargo en el Barcelona. “Con todos he tenido una relación profesional y personal muy buena. He aprendido muchísimo de ellos. Seguramente ha sido la principal fuente de mejora que he tenido”, afirma. Obseso del trabajo de equipo, antes de conseguir el récord, Martínez no se olvida del que tiene en casa. “De mi familia, pero sobre todo de mi mujer. Somos un equipo. Así lo he sentido yo siempre. Si soy entrenador profesional con una trayectoria tan larga, es por ella. Yo solo no lo hubiera conseguido. Seguro”, dice el técnico, que firmó por el Madrid pocos días después de cumplir 65 años. Hay tiempo para seguir aumentando sus récords.

articles.title: Knicks' Mikal Bridges drills buzzer-beating 3-pointer to defeat Trail Blazers
articles.summary: Perhaps the shot is a harbinger of a Bridges bounce-back, as he's struggled early in the 2026-27 campaign.
articles.body:
The New York Knicks are rounding into form, and maybe Saturday night is what Mikal Bridges needed to get back on track, too.

The 30-year-old wing, who came into a matchup with the Portland Trail Blazers shooting just north of 40% from the field and a smidge above 30% from deep, drilled a buzzer-beating 3-pointer to deliver New York a 97-96 victory in Madison Square Garden.

Bridges finished with 12 points on 5-of-8 shooting. He connected on two of his three attempts from long range. The last one extended the Knicks' win streak to four games.

Following a pair of Deni Avdija free throws that put the Trail Blazers (10-6) up 96-94, New York (10-6) took a timeout. With 3.2 seconds remaining, Josh Hart inbounded the ball to Bridges.

He caught the pass to the right of the top of the arc, used a quick fake to get an overzealous Toumani Camara to bite, took one more dribble and launched.

The ball rattled in, the buzzer sounded and Mike Breen exclaimed, "Bang! Bang!"

Bridges was swarmed by his Knicks teammates, eventually wearing a smile as MSG reveled in utter pandemonium.

He came to the rescue on a night when New York squandered a 26-point lead. The Knicks shot 13 of 27 from 3-point land in the first half but scored only 31 points over the final two quarters.

Bridges admitted afterward that Portland played "harder" than New York in the second half.

But he also noted in that on-court postgame interview: "It's 48 minutes. We just kept persevering through the time and ended up winning the game."

After trailing 94-84 with less than five minutes to go, the Trail Blazers went on a 12-0 run, which culminated in the aforementioned Avdija free throws. Additionally, that stretch featured a game-tying 3-pointer from Damian Lillard.

Avdija was sent to the line because of a head-scratching foul by Knicks center Andre Drummond, who switched and committed the personal on the floor well beyond the arc .

Avdija had 20 points. Center Donovan Clingan spearheaded Portland's effort with 22 points and 13 rebounds. Lillard put up just 15 points and shot a meager 1 of 9 from outside.

New York was paced by Jalen Brunson's 30 points. Fellow guard Landry Shamet poured in 20 points.

Bridges, though, was the hero, sinking a redemptive shot 16 games into what's been a trying season for the ninth-year pro.

articles.title: NCAA women's tourney will reportedly no longer require pregame handshakes after Geno Auriemma-Dawn Staley confrontation
articles.summary: Auriemma infamously blew up on Staley at the end of UConn's Final Four defeat to South Carolina last season, voicing frustration about her not showing up for...
articles.body:
The NCAA women's basketball tournament won't be mandating pregame handshakes anymore, according to multiple reports Saturday that cited a memo sent by the Division I women's basketball committee to administrators of all D-I programs.

In the memo, the committee reportedly "encourages" coaches to still shake hands informally prior to team introductions at the NCAA tournament, but those handshakes will no longer be required.

The change comes after pregame handshakes became a source of controversy during last season's Final Four. UConn head coach Geno Auriemma infamously blew up on South Carolina head coach Dawn Staley at the end of the Huskies' national semifinal defeat to the Gamecocks.

With less than a second left on the clock, Auriemma approached Staley on the sideline and voiced his grievances, including his frustration about her not showing up for a specific pregame handshake. He initiated what became a heated exchange that ultimately needed to be split up.

While video and photographs documented a pregame handshake between Staley and Auriemma , the 12-time national champion head coach took issue with Staley not showing up for another handshake at center court during in-arena coach introductions after the starting lineups.

At that particular moment, Staley remained in the South Carolina huddle. Meanwhile, Auriemma stood near the scorer's table before heading back toward his bench.

"I waited there for like three minutes," Auriemma said postgame. "So it is what it is."

The following day, Auriemma issued the first of his two apology statements . In his second one, he addressed Staley by name and expressed more remorse about the incident, even confessing, "I lost myself."

Staley, a three-time national champion head coach herself, gave Auriemma grace in the fallout of the situation, even writing that one moment "doesn't change the impact he's had on growing women's basketball."

The 2027 NCAA tournament will include 76 teams, as will be the case on the men's side. In the women's tourney, the opening round and first and second rounds will continue to be hosted on campus sites. Next year's regional sites are Philadelphia and Las Vegas. The Final Four will take place in Columbus, Ohio.

articles.title: Wembanyama se inventa una burrada con 18 minutos de pura dominación
articles.standfirst: Firma ante los Pelicans el tercer partido de su carrera con 50 puntos
articles.summary: Firma ante los Pelicans el tercer partido de su carrera con 50 puntos
articles.body: Victor Wembanyama hizo una demostración de dominación absoluta del baloncesto destrozando a los New Orleans Pelicans en una primera parte que ya forma parte de la historia de la NBA. El jugador de los Spurs firmó una línea estadística al decanso que ningún otro jugador ha logrado en la temporada en un partido completo (ni por ningçun jugador en una primera mitad en la era del 'jugada a jugada': 32 puntos, 12 rebotes, tres tapones tres robos. Fue la aportación de francés en 18 minutos de juego memorables para impulsar a su equipo a la victoria, 114-91, sobre unos Pelicans que pierden su noveno partido en los últimos 10. Más tarde, Wemby acabó con 50 puntos, 19 rebotes, cinco tapones y cuatro robos, reconociendo que había inflado su estadísticas cuando su entrenador, Mitch Johnson, le dijo que le quedaba un minuto y medio en la cancha para llegar a los 50: "Le dije: puede ser tiempo suficiente". Y acertó el galo. En un perido de un minuto y 14 segundos, Wemby clavó dos triples para dejar a su equipo con un claro 108-82 antes de que el rookie Tarris Reed Jr. saliera por él. Había llegado a los 50 por tercera vez en su carrera. "Solo quiero seguir sumándolas", dijo sobre la cantidad de actuaciones históricas que ha protagonizado en su carrera. "No es algo que me proponga hacer; simplemente surgen cuando jugamos de la manera correcta como equipo. Ojalá vengan muchas más". La actuación de Wemby, claro, ya es historia de la NBA. Iguala a LeBron James y Devin Booker como segundo jugador con más actuaciones de 50 puntos o más a la edad de 22 años y se une a la leyenda de su equipo, David Robinson, como los únicos jugadores en la historia con múltiples partidos de 50 puntos y cinco tapones desde que esta última estadística fui incluida de forma oficial en 1973-74. Y hay más. Es el primero que desde esa fecha, acumula cuatro robos y más de 15 rebotes además de los puntos (50) y los tapones (5). Desde 1979-80, con la introducción del triples, es el primero en firmar un +50 en puntos, +5 en tapones con cinco o más triples. Se une a un grupo con Anthony Davis, Bob McAdoo y Wilt Chamberlain (que lo hizo cinco veces) con un partido de 50 o más puntos, 15 o más rebotes y cinco o más tapones, en la historia de la NBA. En lo que ya es su tercer partido con 50 o más puntos en su carrera, Wemby firmó por segunda vez una primera mitad alcanzo los 30 puntos y lo hizo con precisión quirúrgica: 12/15 en tiros de campo, con 3/5 en triples, dominando las dos zonas con 13 rebotes. Todo eso, en 18 minutos. A dos minutos para el descanso, Wemby llevaba más puntos que todos los titulares de los Pelicans juntos. En esa primera parte inolvidable, Wemby dedicó uno de sus triples a la actriz Selena Gómez, presente entre los 18.708 aficionados del Frost Bank Center. "Claro, me tuve que llucir ante ella", dijo el galo con una sonrisa preguntado sobre este hecho al final del partido.

articles.title: NBA star Kyle Kuzma gives his take on moon landing conspiracy theory
articles.summary: Milwaukee Bucks forward Kyle Kuzma has questioned whether the United States ever landed astronauts on the Moon, describing footage from the Apollo missions a...
articles.body:
Milwaukee Bucks forward Kyle Kuzma has questioned whether the United States ever landed astronauts on the Moon, describing footage from the Apollo missions as "B*" during an appearance on his podcast.

The former Los Angeles Lakers star shared his views while speaking with entrepreneur Anthony Pompliano on Read the Room , where the pair discussed technology, business and space exploration.

Kuzma suggested there was "no chance" humans had reached the lunar surface during the original missions, despite the extensive historical and scientific evidence supporting them.

Kyle Kuzma questions whether NASA really landed astronauts on the Moon

Explaining his doubts, Kuzma said: "Well, I just, the footage is just B* to me. Like why haven't we gone back?"

He continued: "You know, I think, you know, we've been around, you know, might have been in orbit, you know, Artemis happened. Obviously, you know, that's a true statement, but I just don't think back then that necessarily happened."

NASA first landed astronauts on the Moon during Apollo 11 in 1969. Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin became the first humans to walk on its surface, while Michael Collins remained in lunar orbit.

Five further Apollo missions successfully landed astronauts, with Apollo 17 completing the final crewed lunar landing in 1972. Evidence also extends beyond television footage, including scientific equipment left on the Moon that is still used for research.

Interestingly, Kuzma's doubts about the Apollo missions have not stopped him from showing an interest in future lunar exploration.

Taking to X, the Bucks forward predicted that humans would return to the Moon within the next few years.

"We will be on the moon no question by '29-30," Kuzma uttered.

He also imagined what playing basketball on the lunar surface might look like, suggesting the lower gravity could make for a very different experience.

"I can only imagine basketball on the moon. That'd be a very slow-paced game. I think you could play the game of basketball forever on the moon, essentially."

Kuzma is not the first high-profile athlete to question the Moon landings, with Stephen Curry previously raising similar doubts before clarifying that he was joking.

For now, the Bucks star appears more interested in what humanity could achieve next than accepting what happened during the Apollo era.

articles.title: El Barça no gana para disgustos: Nebo, tres o cuatro meses de baja
articles.standfirst: El pívot sufrió una avulsión parcial del tendón rotuliano de la rodilla derecha en el encuentro del pasado viernes de Euroliga ante el Estrella Roja.
articles.summary: El pívot sufrió una avulsión parcial del tendón rotuliano de la rodilla derecha en el encuentro del pasado viernes de Euroliga ante el Estrella Roja.
articles.body: El Barça se enfrenta a un nuevo y duro contratiempo en una temporada que empieza a convertirse en una auténtica carrera de obstáculos. Josh Nebo estará entre tres y cuatro meses de baja después de sufrir una avulsión parcial del tendón rotuliano de la rodilla derecha durante el encuentro del pasado viernes ante el Estrella Roja. Una lesión importante que supone un golpe de consideración para los planes del conjunto azulgrana y que obligará al pívot estadounidense a seguir un tratamiento conservador. La enfermería culé no da tregua. A la larga ausencia de Nebo se suma ahora la de Tyrese Martin, que no estará disponible para el compromiso de este domingo frente a La Laguna Tenerife por un empeoramiento de las molestias en el tobillo derecho. El alero sufrió un esguince el pasado martes ante el París Basketball y, aunque llegó a disputar el choque contra el Estrella Roja, no ha podido recuperarse a tiempo. Tampoco podrá echar una mano de momento Killian Hayes. El reciente fichaje azulgrana continúa con su proceso de puesta a punto y todavía no está preparado para entrar en la convocatoria. Ante este panorama, el joven Abdu Kone será el encargado de completar la lista para el partido, en una nueva muestra de las dificultades que está teniendo el Barça para mantener a toda su plantilla disponible. Los problemas físicos se han convertido en un auténtico quebradero de cabeza para el cuerpo técnico, que sigue acumulando bajas en un calendario cada vez más exigente. A los contratiempos de Nebo y Martin se unen los de Umoja Gibson, Kevin Punter, Tosan Evbuomwan y Yoan Makoundou. Una plaga de lesiones que amenaza con condicionar seriamente la temporada azulgrana y que obliga al equipo a multiplicar esfuerzos para sobrevivir a una situación cada vez más complicada.

articles.title: Norman Powell Injured, Latest on Bulls Star's Timeline to Return from Hamstring Diagnosis
articles.summary: Chicago Bulls guard Norman Powell suffered a "mild right hamstring strain" during Friday's 98-94 loss against the Washington Wizards, the team announced Sunday, and will be "reevaluated later this week."
articles.body:
Chicago Bulls guard Norman Powell suffered a "mild right hamstring strain" during Friday's 98-94 loss against the Washington Wizards, the team announced Sunday, and will be "reevaluated later this week."

Powell had 16 points, three rebounds and two assists across 33 minutes during the contest. He was the team's leading scorer in the loss.

He is also Chicago's leading scorer on the season, putting up 20.8 points to go along with 2.8 rebounds, 2.4 assists and 1.4 steals per game.

Granted, it has come during a rough season for the Bulls. While the team has recently looked better, winning three of its last five, a 1-9 start to the season may have doomed any playoff hopes right out of the gate.

There have been some positives. Namely, rookie big man Caleb Wilson (18.9 PPG, 6.2 RPG) looks like a star in the making and headlines a promising young core that also includes Josh Giddey, Jalen Smith, Matas Buzelis and Noa Essengue.

But the Bulls will likely be sellers come February and because Powell is essentially on an expiring contract—he does have a $22.5 million team option for next season that could be declined—he'll be of interest to contenders ahead of this year's trade deadline. Any team needing a dose of instant offense in the backcourt will likely be on the phone with the Bulls, inquiring about the 33-year old.

In the meantime, look for players like Tre Jones and Buddy Hield to play a bigger role in the backcourt while Powell is out injured.

articles.title: Devin Booker Gives Darryn Peterson Signed Jersey to 'My Fav Rook' in New Photo of Surprise Gift
articles.summary: Despite Friday's 111-101 loss to the Phoenix Suns, Utah Jazz rookie guard Darryn Peterson impressed star sharpshooter Devin Booker.
articles.body:
Despite Friday's 111-101 loss to the Phoenix Suns, Utah Jazz rookie guard Darryn Peterson impressed star sharpshooter Devin Booker.

After dropping 20 points, 10 rebounds and eight assists, the 2026 No. 2 pick was surprised with a signed jersey from Booker that included a special message.

"Stay on the Gas! My fav rook!" Booker wrote.

Peterson told reporters that Booker is one of his favorite players and someone he models his game after.

"I think I got some stops," Peterson said after the game. "The fan goes out the window when we guard them, and we're playing. Definitely going to see if they got some pictures of me guarding him or something. It's always cool."

Peterson and Booker will meet on the court again later this month when the Jazz and Suns face off on Nov. 29.

articles.title: Dejounte Murray Hasn't Been to Pelicans Arena Since Trade Request, Latest NBA Rumors on Suns Talks
articles.summary: After requesting a trade from the New Orleans Pelicans, veteran guard Dejounte Murray has already said his goodbyes to the franchise.
articles.body:
After requesting a trade from the New Orleans Pelicans, veteran guard Dejounte Murray has already said his goodbyes to the franchise.

Rod Walker of The Times-Picayune reported that Murray "hasn't set foot in the Smoothie King Center since" his trade request, and he "almost certainly won't ever wear a Pelicans uniform again."

Walker added that a source said New Orleans has been "in constant talks with the Phoenix Suns," but "other than that, there haven't been many other teams calling about Murray."

It was just over a week ago that Murray's trade request became public, with the Pelicans confirming that they are working with his representatives to find a resolution.

"Today, Dejounte Murray's representatives informed us of his request to be traded," the Pelicans said in a statement on Nov. 13. "We will evaluate potential trade opportunities that are in the best interest of our organization."

However, with Murray making $32.8 million this season and holding a $30.8 million player option for 2027-28, teams aren't lining up to acquire the disgruntled guard. New Orleans sent two first-round picks, Dyson Daniels, Larry Nance Jr. and E.J. Liddell to the Atlanta Hawks to acquire Murray in 2024, so the team doesn't want to lose him for nothing. The source Walker spoke to added that the Pelicans "aren't going to be in a hurry to make a trade."

This leaves Murray sitting at home while New Orleans moves forward without him. The Pelicans fell to 5-13 this season with Saturday's 114-91 loss to the San Antonio Spurs and will be back in action on Monday night against the Suns, who don't appear very driven to trade for Murray.

articles.title: Armoni Brooks aúpa al Valencia y troncha la resistencia del Río Breogán en un partidazo
articles.standfirst: El alero puso la guinda al desmelene ofensivo en el Roig Arena con 11 de sus 21 puntos en el último cuarto
articles.summary: El alero puso la guinda al desmelene ofensivo en el Roig Arena con 11 de sus 21 puntos en el último cuarto
articles.body: El Valencia Basket se impuso al Río Breogán este domingo (129-111) en un partido que decidió a su favor en el último cuarto con el acierto del exterior Armoni Brooks, que anotó 11 de sus 21 puntos en el definitivo parcial, y en el que celebró su 40 aniversario luciendo una camiseta homenaje a su primera etapa en 1986. El conjunto 'taronja', además, firmó la máxima anotación de su historia con los 129 puntos anotados en un partido en el que ambos equipos demostraron desde el inicio su capacidad ofensiva. Tercer y segundo máximos anotadores de la liga, respectivamente, los dos convirtieron los primeros minutos en una exhibición anotadora. Los triples y el acierto de Mario Saint-Supéry eran respondidos por los puntos de Mihajlo Andric y de Josep Peris. Solo la irrupción de Gonzalo Corbalán y de Álvaro Cárdenas, incisivos con sus penetraciones, parecían darle un ritmo mayor al Valencia Basket (20-15, min.5). Pero los cambios también funcionaron en el Breogán. Francis Alonso firmó 7 puntos en 6 minutos para recuperar el ritmo anotador y solo un triple de Kameron Taylor sobre la bocina pudo romper el empate (31-29, min.10). En busca de controlar el partido, el Valencia Basket trató de activarse en defensa y fruto de su mejoría atrás encontró canastas fáciles. Armoni Brooks firmó un tapón, un triple y un 'alley oop' que levantaron al Roig Arena e impulsaron a su equipo, que llegaría a alcanzar la máxima diferencia con un triple de Dylan Osetkowski (44-35, min. 14). Fueron los mejores minutos de un conjunto 'taronja' que había desconectado al Breogán. Más incómodos, los visitantes se agarraron a la inspiración de Andric, que, con dos triples seguidos, lideró un pequeño parcial de 0-6 que volvía a reducir la distancia y que obligó al técnico 'taronja', Xavi Albert, a pedir tiempo muerto. El parón conectó de nuevo a los suyos. Con canastas cerca del aro de Neal Sako y de Kameron Taylor, la diferencia se disparó hasta los 12 puntos y los 'taronja' se fueron al descanso con una marcha anotadora más (61-51, min.20). El Valencia Basket mantuvo ese ritmo tras el descanso con claro protagonismo para Nikola Mirotic. En menos de cuatro minutos anotó 10 puntos, 5 de ellos seguidos, para llevar la distancia a los 15. La salida en tromba del Valencia Basket siguió superando a un Breogán que empezaba a lamentar la escasa producción ofensiva de su principal referente, el exterior Rasir Bolton. Además, cada canasta que anotaba era devuelta. Si Tevin Brown y Andersson García castigaban desde el triple, Brooks y Corbalán devolvían el golpe. Parecía que los visitantes se quedaban atrás, pero en su momento más complicado fueron capaces de reengancharse con un parcial de 1-10 gracias a los triples de Dominik Mavra y Aleksandar Aranitovic y dejarlo todo abierto para el último cuarto (90-85, min. 30). El Valencia Basket trató de romper definitivamente el partido nada más arrancar el último acto. Un parcial de 10-3 con los triples de Brooks y Mirotic volvieron a poner una distancia reseñable de 12 puntos, pero todavía con 8 minutos por jugar. El Breogán ya había demostrado su capacidad de resistencia, pero Brooks se encargó de evitar cualquier reacción. El exterior 'taronja' anotó 11 puntos con tres triples y sirvió en bandeja la canasta que llevó la distancia a los 16 puntos, convertida por Corbalán tras una recuperación del propio Brooks (109-93, min.34). Ya con el partido controlado, el Valencia Basket se dedicó a mantener su ventaja y a seguir anotando hasta alcanzar los 129 puntos, su nueva mejor anotación y marca que superó los 127 anotados ante el Leyma Coruña en la temporada 2024-2025. 129.- Valencia Basket (31+30+29+39): Shorts (17), Saint-Supèry (13), Taylor (13), Mirotic (15), Sako (2) -cinco inicial- Gueye (6), Brooks (21), Moore (8), Corbalán (17), Puerto (3), Cárdenas (3), Osetkowski (11). 111.- Río Breogán (29+22+34+26): Bolton (10), Peris (10), Brown (7), Andric (18), Kasibabu (-) -cinco inicial- Alonso (18), García (12), Brimah (3), Aranitovic (8), Mavra (13), Brankovic (12), Quintela (-). articles.title: Emotivo homenaje del madridismo al legendario Lolo Sainz
articles.standfirst: El mítico entrenador, recibió una ovación antológica en el descanso del Madrid-Joventut en el que Florentino Pérez le entregó un trofeo y una camiseta conmemorativa
articles.summary: El mítico entrenador, recibió una ovación antológica en el descanso del Madrid-Joventut en el que Florentino Pérez le entregó un trofeo y una camiseta conmemorativa
articles.body: Manuel 'Lolo' Sainz, exjugador y ex entrenador del Real Madrid de baloncesto, recibió un caluroso homenaje en el Movistar Arena por parte de la afición del club blanco en el descanso del encuentro de la novena jornada de la Liga Endesa que enfrenta a este contra el Asisa Joventut. Sainz saltó al parqué en solitario y, en mitad de la pista, recibió los aplausos de la grada poco antes de que todos los presentes pudieran ver, a través de los marcadores, un vídeo con algunos de sus mejores momentos. Acto seguido salió a su encuentro el presidente Florentino Pérez, quien le hizo entrega de un trofeo con forma del escudo del Real Madrid y de una camiseta de la actual temporada con su apellido y el dorsal número siete. Mientras, desde la grada, se coreó 'Lolo, Lolo'. Como jugador Sainz ganó cuatro Copas de Europa, 7 Ligas y 5 Copas, además de ser internacional con la selección española en 68 ocasiones; y durante sus 14 temporadas como técnico de la entidad sumó dos Copas de Europa más, 8 Ligas, 4 Copas de España, 2 Recopas, 4 Intercontinentales, 1 Korac y 1 Supercopa de España, firmando 595 victorias en 734 partidos. Asimismo entrenó al propio Joventut, fue seleccionador español logrando una medalla continental en 1999, y ejerció como director general de la sección de baloncesto del Real Madrid durante tres años.

articles.title: Joe Lunardi 2027 Bracketology for Top Seeds, Bubble Teams After Michigan Loses to Unranked Villanova
articles.summary: ESPN bracketologist Joe Lunardi updated his ongoing look at the potential NCAA men's tournament field on Sunday, with very few changes across his projected top 16 seeds.
articles.body:
ESPN bracketologist Joe Lunardi updated his ongoing look at the potential NCAA men's tournament field on Sunday, with very few changes across his projected top 16 seeds.

Michigan is still hovering around the 5-seed range following its 79-73 loss against unranked Villanova on Saturday, the Wolverines' second loss of the early season. The Wildcats, meanwhile, are one of Lunardi's last four in.

Now, as Lunardi would probably tell you himself, take all of this with a grain of salt. It's early days, with March still several months away. It does seem likely that the teams at the top of the rankings will remain contenders, given the talent on hand, but a lot can change before March Madness.

One thing is for certain at the moment—Houston is the team to beat after a huge week that saw them knock off both Florida and Kansas. The Cougars are for real.

articles.title: La Laguna Tenerife resiste y acaba diluyendo al Barcelona
articles.standfirst: Hunter (20 puntos y 9 rebotes) comanda el trabajado triunfo tinerfeño
articles.summary: Hunter (20 puntos y 9 rebotes) comanda el trabajado triunfo tinerfeño
articles.body: Gran trabajo de resistencia y fe de un La Laguna Tenerife que aguantó este domingo las acometidas del Barça, que consiguió irse nueve puntos arriba de los canarios antes del descanso. Los de Lakovic mantuvieron el hilo del encuentro y reaccionaron para remontar y dominar en el último tramo a los visitantes y cerraron el marcador con una diferencia de 12 puntos. Vertiginoso primer cuarto vivido en el Santiago Martín, que sirvió de aviso para lo que estaba por venir en una gran tarde de baloncesto correspondiente a la novena jornada de Liga Endesa, en la que La Laguna Tenerife y Barça se dejaron absolutamente todo para mantener viva la pelea con Valencia Basket para esa segunda plaza en la clasificación. En estos primeros diez minutos no se vio un marcador que sobrepasaba los dos puntos de ventaja para uno u otro hasta pasado el minuto siete de juego en el que el Barça se fue cuatro arriba. Tras dos tiros libres convertidos de Balcerowski, que puso el 11-15 en el electrónico. Pero la rápida reacción de Hunter y, posteriormente, el triple de Abromaitis devolvieron a los canaristas a la mínima diferencia hasta conseguir darle la vuelta y cerrar el cuarto con un 22-21. Sekulic apretó a los suyos y el Barça firmó un segundo cuarto muy sólido, en el que presentó una defensa más férrea, pero sobre todo un ataque más agresivo, con lo que consiguió bajar levemente la conversión de los locales y aumentar la suya y, además, de una manera muy temprana. El paso por vestuarios revivió a La Laguna Tenerife de manera evidente, ya que ingresó de nuevo al parqué con una solvencia sobresaliente, con un parcial inicial de 8-0 gracias a dos triples de Guy y un tiro en suspensión de Van Beck, que supuso la remontada local y el estallido de un Santiago Martín que no dejó de apretar en toda la tarde, siendo un jugador más para los suyos. Guy siguió a lo suyo y aumentó el registro a ocho puntos anotados en apenas dos minutos y medio (50-49), lo que metió de lleno a los canaristas en el partido y fue el punto de inflexión clave para que la contienda terminase de la manera que lo hizo, gracias en gran parte al desempeño del estadounidense que firmó un encuentro superlativo, aunque está empezando a regularizar este imponente nivel. Sekulic se vio obligado a parar esta dinámica con un tiempo muerto que su equipo aprovechó notablemente al volver con un parcial de 0-9 e instalar un 55-59 a falta de 4:40 para el cierre del tercer cuarto. Lejos de sembrar la incertidumbre en las arcas del equipo aurinegro activó de nuevo el buen juego de los locales, que consiguieron volver a darle vuelta a la contienda y apuntar un 68-67 con un triple de Doornekamp a falta de diez segundos. Con el espectáculo servido y todo por decidirse, La Laguna Tenerife y Barça se midieron en un épico cuarto cuarto, en el que los de Jaka Lakovic impusieron su juego y dominaron visiblemente a los azulgrana hasta llegar al 94-82 final. 94 La Laguna Tenerife (22+18+28+26): Jaime Fernández (9), Van Beck (16), Shermadini (2), Alderete (2), Doornekamp (8) -inicial-, Guy (26), Diego Rodríguez (-), Prekevicius (-), Abromaitis (8), Sangare (-), Hunter (20), Kurucs (3). 82 Barça (21+26+20+15): Robinson (4), Brizuela (9), Minaya (5), Kone (10), Parra (7) -inicial-, Umude (3), Ubal (15), Nkamhoua (4), Núñez (9), Balcerowski (16). articles.title: New WNBA Mock Draft 2027 Drops from Top Experts amid JuJu Watkins & Hannah Hidalgo Speculation
articles.summary: In the event USC star JuJu Watkins returns to the Trojans for one more season, a new consensus No. 1 pick in the 2027 WNBA draft will emerge.
articles.body:
In the event USC star JuJu Watkins returns to the Trojans for one more season, a new consensus No. 1 pick in the 2027 WNBA draft will emerge.

The Athletic's Sabreena Merchant, Chantel Jennings and Annie Costabile forecasted the first round in a scenario where Watkins, Notre Dame guard Hannah Hidalgo and UCLA forward Addy Brown all turn down the chance to go pro.

Costabile wrote that selecting Texas forward Madison Booker "seems like an easy decision" for the Toronto Tempo. LSU guard Mikaylah Williams was next off the board to the Houston Comets.

*JuJu Watkins, Hannah Hidalgo and Addy Brown were ineligible for selection

The Tempo would be disappointed to lose out on Watkins, who hasn't missed a beat after coming back from a torn ACL. She's averaging 36.8 points and 3.6 assists through her first five games.

Booker is somebody Toronto could build the franchise around, though. The 6'1" forward continues to be a pillar of consistency. She's averaging 18.8 points, 5.0 rebounds, 4.0 assists and 2.3 steals.

Bleacher Report's Jack Bonin compared Booker to five-time All-Star Jackie Young and said there would be plenty of years where she'd be the top player on the board.

Recent history doesn't provide strong evidence one way or the other as to what Watkins, Hidalgo and the other big stars with remaining eligibility will decide.

Aliyah Boston and Caitlin Clark both entered the draft when they were the heavy favorites to go No. 1 in 2023 and 2024. Paige Bueckers, however, wanted to chase a national title at UConn and put off the WNBA for a year. Olivia Miles could've been a top-five selection in 2025 but waited until the following season.

Teams with high picks next spring are stuck in a tough spot. The Tempo and Comets in particular have to basically draw up a Plan B, C and D in case Watkins, Hidalgo and/or Booker remove themselves from the draft pool.

As long as all three don't forgo the draft, the talent at the top should still be pretty strong.

articles.title: Gabe Vincent, Kings Reportedly Agree to Contract as Darius Acuff Jr.'s Backup, Updated Depth Chart
articles.summary: The Sacramento Kings are reportedly signing veteran guard Gabe Vincent, according to ESPN's Shams Charania, giving impressive rookie Darius Acuff Jr. a backup on the depth chart.
articles.body:
The Sacramento Kings are reportedly signing veteran guard Gabe Vincent, according to ESPN's Shams Charania , giving impressive rookie Darius Acuff Jr. a backup on the depth chart.

Here's a look at the team's current roster:

PG: Darius Acuff Jr. / Gabe Vincent / Emanuel Sharp

SG: Zach LaVine / Malik Monk / Daeqwon Plowden

C: Domantas Sabonis / Dylan Cardwell / Mason Plumlee

Insiders Sound Off on Acuff's Playing Style

Vincent, 30, appeared in 53 games between the Los Angeles Lakers and the Atlanta Hawks, averaging 4.4 points and 1.4 assists per game.

Since being an important role player for the Miami Heat in his first four seasons—he'll forever be remembered in Miami for his strong performance in the team's run to the NBA Finals in the 2022-23 season, averaging 12.7 points and 3.5 assists—he's dealt with injuries and largely been buried at the back of several rotations.

In Sacramento, however, he'll have a chance to earn more minutes. The Kings haven't had a natural backup for Acuff beyond Sharp, a rookie second-rounder.

The 2-14 Kings haven't had many bright spots beyond Acuff either. The electric young point guard is averaging 25.4 points and 7.4 assists per game this season and looks like a potential superstar. The Kings have a real franchise cornerstone on their hands.

But they the rest of the roster has been a mismatch of veterans the Kings would probably prefer to trade and younger players trying to find their way. One would imagine the team would be sellers ahead of the February deadline if they can find takers for players like Hunter, LaVine, Sabonis and Monk.

For the time being, Vincent will offer a bit more veteran depth.

articles.title: Rockets Make Roster Move With G League Recall
articles.summary: The Houston Rockets have had many injuries so far this season in both their frontcourt and backcourt. Houston has recalled guard Bruce Thornton from their NB...
articles.body:
The Houston Rockets have had many injuries so far this season in both their frontcourt and backcourt. Houston has recalled guard Bruce Thornton from their NBA G League affiliate, Rio Grande Valley, per the RGV Vipers X account. As of right now, no one in their backcourt is injured, and they are all expected to play. This call-up may be to give him some experience in practice with them, or maybe even to get in the game and get some playing time.

Why Rockets Brought Bruce Thornton Back to the NBA

The Rockets brought Thornton back to the NBA because the Vipers don't play again until Saturday. This gives him a chance to train with the NBA guys and maybe see some minutes. If Houston is blowing out any of their opponents this week or an injury occurs, Thornton could find himself getting valuable minutes. This is big for a rookie like him.

In college, Thornton was a ball-dominant guard who could score from all over. He could attack the paint, shoot mid-range shots, and knock down threes. His play could be important this week to provide another scorer for this team. This week will be important for Thornton to prove that he belongs in the NBA, and this is a chance for him to show it.

What This Move Could Mean For Houston's Guard Rotation

The rotation of the Rockets most likely won't see any changes barring any injuries. If games are close, Thornton may not see much time and will most likely watch from the bench. All the guards that Houston has are already established and have made a name for themselves; Thornton is still trying to get there. It's better to have him with the NBA team training while the affiliate won't have a game until Saturday.

This call-up doesn't mean anything big for the time being. It may just be to get him some experience while the Vipers don't have a game. This is a move that will help Thornton in the long run. He is a player who's better to have on the bench just in case, because this Houston team has dealt with a lot of injuries so far. Thornton will have a chance to improve his game this week.

articles.title: Geno Auriemma, Dawn Staley Haven't Spoken Since Viral Video from UConn-South Carolina Final Four
articles.summary: When UConn and South Carolina met in the Final Four last year, the game ended with a heated interaction between head coaches Geno Auriemma and Dawn Staley.
articles.body:
When UConn and South Carolina met in the Final Four last year, the game ended with a heated interaction between head coaches Geno Auriemma and Dawn Staley.

Auriemma, the head coach of the Huskies, said the two haven't spoken since then, but he doesn't want their relationship to be the focus of Tuesday's meeting.

"I'm not playing, so I'm just trying to coach my team because they're the ones playing," Auriemma told reporters Sunday. "And that's what people are coming to watch, I think. They're coming to watch South Carolina and Connecticut play against each other."

He added: "I don't coach against other coaches. I coach against their players."

The Gamecocks won the Final Four matchup 62-48, handing UConn its only loss of the season. As the game ended, Auriemma and Staley met to shake hands, and he confronted her.

Staley said in a postgame interview that she wasn't aware of what she did to offend Auriemma.

"I have no idea, but I'm gonna let you know this. I'm of integrity. I'm of integrity," Staley said. "So if I did something wrong to Geno, I had no idea what I did. I guess he thought I didn't shake his hand at the beginning of the game.

"I didn't know. I went down there pregame, shook everybody on his staff's hands. I don't know what he came with after the game, but hey, sometimes things get heated. We move on."

Auriemma didn't go into detail about the interaction in his postgame press conference.

"I said what I had to say," Auriemma told reporters. "Nothing. Nothing."

"There's no excuse for how I handled the end of the game vs. South Carolina," he said . "It's unlike what I do and what our standard is here at Connecticut. I want to apologize to the staff and the team at South Carolina. It was uncalled for in how I reacted. The story should be how well South Carolina played, and I don't want my actions to detract from that. I've had a great relationship with their staff, and I sincerely want to apologize to them."

Auriemma has been known to let his anger get the best of him in the past, and that certainly was the case after losing to the Gamecocks last April. He'll look to avoid another situation like that when UConn and South Carolina meet on Tuesday.

articles.title: Iowa State Will Have 'Enhanced Monitoring' of Women's Basketball After Ex-Players Seek Review
articles.summary: AMES, Iowa (AP) — The Iowa State women's basketball team will have "enhanced monitoring," the school announced in a statement that came in the wake of a letter from six former players asking the university for an independent review of coach Bill Fennelly's program.
articles.body:
AMES, Iowa (AP) — The Iowa State women's basketball team will have "enhanced monitoring," the school announced in a statement that came in the wake of a letter from six former players asking the university for an independent review of coach Bill Fennelly's program.

The statement didn't offer specifics on what new steps would be taken to monitor the program.

"Iowa State University cares deeply about the health and well-being of our student-athletes and takes seriously any claims of conduct contrary to our values and standards," the school said Saturday in the statement. "The university has appropriate policies and procedures in place to address allegations of misconduct. Iowa State has reached out to the attorney representing the former women's basketball student-athletes to try and ascertain details of their general claims.

Geno, Dawn Haven't Spoke Since Final Four 😬

"In the meantime, to best live up to our mission and to support our student-athletes as well as Coach Fennelly and his coaching staff, we have instituted enhanced monitoring of the women's basketball program."

Fennelly said after his team beat Drake on Sunday to remain undefeated that he didn't know what the "enhanced monitoring" meant and hasn't been told specifically anything about it. He said he heard about the letter from the former players from the school's lawyers.

"Disappointed, obviously, confused a little bit. My focus and I know this sounds cliche, I'm 100% focused on our team. I can't control other stuff. I know that sounds boring and sounds whatever, it's the absolute truth," Fennelly said. "My head is down and I'm focused on the 13 kids in that locker room and the coaches."

The former players said they asked for the review after Fennelly's one-game suspension for "inappropriate contact" with a player. He nudged Sienna Harvey's head with his hand in a win over UIC a week ago. Fennelly later apologized for the incident. He served the suspension on Wednesday when Iowa State beat Northern Iowa.

Harvey said after that game that she and her teammates have "a great relationship" with coach Fennelly.

"I can see how it was perceived on the internet, but he loves us and cares about us more than anyone," she said. "And I like being coached hard, so I think it was perceived differently than what it was."

The former players said Fennelly's suspension showed what they felt was a long-standing problem in the program. Two of the former players signed their names to the statement while the other four remained anonymous.

"We experienced or witnessed conduct we considered to be verbal, emotional, and psychological abuse from Coach Fennelly," the players wrote in the statement that was sent to numerous media outlets. "We reported this and what we believed was inappropriate physical contact to members of the coaching staff and Iowa State athletic administration, but we do not believe our concerns were taken seriously.

"Our individual experiences may differ, but we are united in our concerns about an environment where intimidation, humiliation, and fear became normalized. For some of us, the consequences did not end with our playing careers. We continue to deal with anxiety, depression, diminished self-worth, and lasting distress that we associate with our time in the program."

Fennelly, 69, announced last month that he would retire at the end of the season , which is his 32nd coaching at the school. He is 662-335 in his career at Iowa State and has made the NCAA Tournament 24 times.

Iowa State lost nine players to the transfer portal including No. 2 all-time scorer Audi Crooks.

articles.title: Amar'e Stoudemire Sworn into Miami-Dade Schools PD, NBA Hall of Famer 'Proud' to Serve Community
articles.summary: NBA Hall of Famer Amar'e Stoudemire has officially been sworn in as an officer with the Miami-Dade Schools Police Department.
articles.body:
NBA Hall of Famer Amar'e Stoudemire has officially been sworn in as an officer with the Miami-Dade Schools Police Department.

"For 18 years, I wore a jersey with my name on the back. Today, I put on a uniform that carries the trust of my community," Stoudemire wrote in a caption on Instagram. "I'm proud to have been sworn in as an officer with the Miami-Dade Schools Police Department. Being entrusted with the safety of our students, educators, and school communities is a responsibility I take to heart."

Stoudemire played 14 seasons in the NBA and was inducted into the Hall of Fame earlier this year.

articles.title: TCU fires Sonny Dykes after giving him a spring extension, and fans' reactions say it all
articles.summary: TCU football fired head coach Sonny Dykes after a 38-17 loss to the Utah Utes, with AD Mike Buddie citing a slide from the Horned Frogs' Fiesta Bowl peak.
articles.body: Seven months after handing Sonny Dykes a massive extension, the powers at TCU decided they'd seen enough. The program let go of the TCU football head coach Sunday, a day after the 38-17 dismantling by the second-ranked Utah Utes. Athletic Director Mike Buddie issued the school's statement, nodding to the 2022 run before laying out the slide since. Saturday marked TCU's final home game of the season. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Since 2022, however, the Frogs have posted a 28-21 overall record and a 17-18 mark in the Big 12 while finishing or ranking 10th or worst in penalty yards per game within the league each of the past four seasons," the statement read, in part. "After appearing in the Big 12 Championship Game in 2022, TCU has finished an average of 7th in the league standings since. With Saturday's result, the Frogs currently sit in 12th." "While Sonny's tenure began with the incredible achievement of winning the 2022 Fiesta Bowl and advancing to the national championship game, the proceeding years have seen our program slide further away from that mountain top than can be accepted," Buddie said. "I am grateful to Sonny for his belief in TCU, his family's love for the Fort Worth community, and for his coaching staff's commitment to recruiting and developing men of high character." COLLEGE FOOTBALL’S JERRY JONES? TEXAS TECH BOOSTER CODY CAMPBELL DEMANDS RETURN ON INVESTMENT "TCU's investment in football has led to dramatic growth of our university and city in the past 20 years, and we cannot allow that investment to fall short of its due return, especially at such a pivotal time of change in college sports. "We expect to compete for Big 12 championships, to be a central figure in the College Football Playoff conversation, and our continued investment and growth potential reflects that. I expect our new leader will echo those sentiments, rally our fan base behind that challenge, and put a team on the field that our alumni, fans, students, and community will be excited to support." Dykes’s five-year stint in Fort Worth opened with a 12-0 regular season behind Max Duggan and a 51-45 Fiesta Bowl upset of Michigan; then the carriage turned to a pumpkin in a 65-7 national championship loss to Georgia. Despite posting 9-4 seasons in 2024 and 2025, a 5-7 slump in 2023 and a 5-6 mark in 2026 sealed his 41-23 tenure. After his dismissal, TCU fans largely anticipated and accepted the move after a stretch of uneven seasons. Reactions on X happily capped the Dykes era. Some memes featured Dave Aranda and Brian Kelly (jokingly) as candidates for the vacancy, while one person suggested Shane Beamer, not so jokingly. "He absolutely caught lightning in a bottle in 2022, and they’ll never reach that height again," one reaction read. More poured in. "Couldn’t wait until after Thursday? Some of us need the Frogs locked in against Texas Tech." Another reacted, "Kinda crazy TCU had the balls to do it." Some took issue with TCU's decision-making on the extension's financials. COLLEGE FOOTBALL’S MEGA ROSTERS AREN’T DELIVERING A RETURN ON INVESTMENT AS LSU, TEXAS A&M AND OREGON PROVE "They extended him in spring for no reason whatsoever. But paying players is what makes CFB broken." OutKick Sr. college sports reporter Trey Wallace gave his first impressions, reading the tea leaves on TCU's next move. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! "They are going to swing for the fences. Could USC head coach Lincoln Riley be interested if things continue trending in that direction in LA? Baylor is interested, so what about TCU? " "A number of names will be interested because of how much TCU is willing to spend in hopes of contending in Big 12 and for CFP spot. They can attract hot names around the sport, and wouldn’t have fired Sonny Dykes if they didn’t already have a few names in mind." FLORIDA STATE FIRES MIKE NORVELL AFTER FAN REVOLT, CLEMSON LOSS SPARK DECISION TO PAY MASSIVE BUYOUT "They will owe him $20 million after giving him an extension in April," Trey noted. articles.title: Watch Klay Thompson's Shoe Break on Video in Strange Play During Heat vs. Thunder
articles.summary: A... shoe timeout?
articles.body:
The Miami Heat had to pause their game against the Oklahoma City Thunder on Sunday when Klay Thompson's shoe broke in a bizarre play.

With 5:04 left in the first quarter, the bottom of Thompson's shoe appeared to break off while he was attempting to defend a transition basket from the Thunder's Ajay Mitchell.

Following the basket, which cut Oklahoma City's deficit to 22-14, Miami head coach Erik Spoelstra called a timeout while officials removed the shoe part from the floor.

Thompson can be seen on the bench lacing up new shoes before getting back on the floor.

articles.title: Wemby Jokes 'Had to Show Off' for Selena Gomez During Historic 50-Point Game for Spurs vs. Pelicans
articles.summary: Victor Wembanyama posted a historic 50 points, 19 rebounds, five blocks and four steals in 32 minutes on Saturday as the San Antonio Spurs blew out the New Orleans Pelicans 114-91.
articles.body:
Victor Wembanyama posted a historic 50 points, 19 rebounds, five blocks and four steals in 32 minutes on Saturday as the San Antonio Spurs blew out the New Orleans Pelicans 114-91.

After the game, he explained he simply had to do it in front of Selena Gomez.

"I had to show off for Selena," Wembanyama told reporters in his postgame media availability.

The "Only Murders in the Building" star is a long-time Spurs fan, and she witnessed Wembanyama become the first player since 1973–74 to record 50 points, 15 rebounds, four steals and five blocks in a single game.

He also became the first player to tally 30 points, 10 rebounds, three blocks and three steals in a game this season.

Gomez is a Texas native and recreated her famous 2016 courtside moment and the Spurs gave her a custom jersey.

articles.title: Player grades: SGA-less Thunder punt in 123-113 loss to Heat
articles.summary: Player grades for the Oklahoma City Thunder's 123-113 loss to the Miami Heat.
articles.body:
Eventually scratched from his first game of the season, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's absence turned this into a skippable watch at worst and background noise at best. The two-time MVP winner went through his pregame warmups, but that was it in his sole visit to one of the most historic gyms in the NBA.

The Oklahoma City Thunder stomached through a 123-113 loss to the Miami Heat . They trailed the entire night and by as many as 20 points.

Before the cross-conference matchup even happened, the Thunder punted it on the front end of road back-to-back. Not only was Gilgeous-Alexander, but so were Jalen Williams, Chet Holmgren, Cason Wallace, Alex Caruso and plenty of other names. To twist the knife, Aday Mara was a very-late scratch, too.

Sure, the Heat were without Giannis Antetokounmpo, but it was a matchup of their B squad butting heads with OKC's C squad. The only Opening Night starter who was suited up for the Thunder was Isaiah Hartenstein. This is the NBA reality they're in right now with their long list of injuries.

Any hopes of a miraculous win popped like a balloon. Not even three minutes in, the Thunder were in an 11-2 deficit. Klay Thompson grilled them from the outside — ala 2016. Ajay Mitchell and Jared McCain tried their best collective carry job, but just didn't have the scoring superpowers to do so. The Thunder were in a 36-24 deficit after the first quarter.

Finally, the Thunder enjoyed some outside shooting luck. Kenrich Williams drained a 3-pointer to make it a single-digit contest. But anytime it felt like OKC was about to go on a run, the Heat answered back with timely outside jumpers. That was the game's flow throughout the first half. The Thunder had 30 points in the second quarter. They entered halftime with a 67-54 deficit.

Bam Adebayo balled out as he flirted with a triple-double. It was the first time this year that he enjoyed first-option hoops. Alas, the second half brought zero intrigue. It was mostly the same as both teams played it out of necessity. Williams had some nice scoring plays, but made costly mistakes as he was asked to be one of their top players. Josh Dix also showed flashes as OKC's best two-way guy with outside makes and good defensive energy.

Mitchell had an epic four-point play. But yeah, that's really it. We're really grasping at straws to find meaty thoughts on this inevitable loss once Gilgeous-Alexander was ruled out. The Thunder had 26 points in the third quarter, but the Heat continued to stiff-arm them on the scoreboard. At that juncture in the game, OKC was in a 95-80 hole. Remember when it had a several-year run as one of the league's top defenses?

If you stayed through this, you're a real NBA trooper. Enjoy whatever online brownie points you can get. The skeleton Thunder gave you every incentive to tune into the NFL Sunday slate instead. The fourth quarter was forgettable as the game got out of hand. OKC put up 33 points in the final frame to pretty up the final score of this wire-to-wire defeat.

The Thunder shot 46% from the field and went 16-of-35 (45.7%) from 3. They shot 13-of-19 on free throws. They had 24 assists on 42 baskets. Six Thunder players scored double-digit points.

Mitchell had 17 points and three assists. McCain finished with 20 points and three assists. Williams tallied 12 points and four rebounds. Bennett Stirtz had a career-best 21 points and five assists. Dix had 13 points and five rebounds. Nique Clifford had 11 points and three rebounds.

Meanwhile, the Heat shot 53% from the field and went 15-of-38 (39.5%) from 3. They shot 18-of-21 on free throws. They had 30 assists on 45 baskets. Seven Heat players scored double-digit points.

Adebayo led the way with a 24-point, 15-rebound and 12-assist triple-double. Pelle Larsson had 21 points and five assists. Nikola Jovic finished with 15 points and eight rebounds. Davion Mitchell tallied 14 points and four rebounds. Bobby Portis Jr. had 10 points and eight rebounds. Ryan Conwell scored 10 points. Simone Fontecchio scored 11 points.

Well, not much to say about this one. It was over as soon as the Thunder ruled out most of their main rotation. I can't believe this is OKC's reality. Just an absolute doomsday scenario. I can feel the fanbase becoming numb to it, so I just wanted to remind folks how surreal this last month has been. Mitchell and McCain have been helpful, but it's clear they're just not guys who can carry for an entire game.

You take this punch on the chin and move on. The Thunder punted this one. I guess the good news is that it happened against an Eastern Conference foe, so the NBA standings and tie-breaking scenarios aren't as consequential. Just get to New Year's. That's all you need to whisper to yourself to cope a little. Because this has just been a brutal stretch of bad basketball from a group that made winning 60-plus look like a walk in the park.

Getting the ball at the top of the key, Mitchell went up for the outside jumper. He splashed it in as Conwell invaded his landing space. The four-point play was one of the rare highlights of a forgettable second half. Sadly, the 24-year-old is showing signs of wear and tear recently.

Mitchell finished with 17 points on 6-of-17 shooting, three assists and three rebounds. He shot 2-of-3 from 3 and went 3-of-5 on free throws. He also had two steals.

As the Southern saying goes — bless your heart. The Thunder have loaded responsibilities on top of responsibilities. To the point that Mitchell is dropping food off his plate. It's just too much to reasonably expect from your projected Sixth Man to be the top scorer on any given night. He tried his best with 11 points in the first half. But was schemed out of the second half as the game got out of hand.

A lot fell on Mitchell's shoulders. He tried to muscle his way to the paint. But to little avail. The jumper was also wishy-washy. He learned what life is like for your average top NBA scoring option. If we're being real here, the Thunder had no shot of generating enough offense to get the shocking upset. They just have way too much talent sidelined right now.

After a hot start as OKC's impromptu Robin, Mitchell has crashed back down to Earth in recent weeks. It's turning out to be too much of a burden to carry. Which is understandable for the 24-year-old. Just a shame that he had such a golden opportunity in front of him to skyrocket his way into top-young-player-in-league talks. Just to struggle with the brute workload associated with that.

On a scramble second-chance look, the Thunder ping-ponged the ball around the perimeter. In one of their halfcourt offensive possessions, Mitchell launched a pass to McCain. He drilled the corner 3-pointer. His outside jumper was one of their rare sources of offense.

McCain finished with 20 points on 7-of-17 shooting, three assists and two rebounds. He shot 2-of-7 from 3 and went 4-of-5 on free throws.

Considering that practically every shot attempt was up for grabs, McCain gladly filled in the vacuum. The 22-year-old has never been gun-shy. It's one of his best qualities as a microwave scorer. Alongside Mitchell, those two helped the Thunder stay within reach in a competitive first half. The second half saw him hunkered down as a scorer.

Considering the circumstances, McCain had the green light to be a nuanced scorer. Not just a catch-and-shoot guy. He sliced through Miami's defense. He also hunted some mid-range looks. His stubborness to go inside the paint also helped him get to the free-throw line. He had 13 points in a super-active first half. Once he cooled off, the Thunder were ran out of the gym.

Just like Mitchell, the Thunder have experimented with McCain's bandwidth. Out of pure necessity. How much of an NBA offense can he carry or scale up to? Well, the last month has proven he's better suited to be a bench scorer. Anything more, it turns into a hit-or-miss situation. Both in the micro within a game and in the macro within a long stretch of games.

Forcing the steal, Williams ran down the floor. He eventually completed the steal-and-score sequence with a driving layup. Amid some of OKC's most apocalyptic runs, the 31-year-old is quietly piling up his best stretch of basketball since the rebuild days. The Thunder have badly needed his production.

Williams finished with 12 points on 5-of-10 shooting, four rebounds and two assists. He shot 2-of-4 from 3 and went 1-of-1 on free throws. He also had one steal.

Considering the circumstances, the Thunder have allowed Williams to lean into his habits. He loves his isolation looks. Something you don't really associate with the team-first guy. But he's proven to have a little bit of a scoring bag that resembles an old-school archetype. That happened here as he barreled his way to the paint and knocked down his outside looks.

Entering the year, Williams was viewed as rich depth. Not somebody who was asked to carry the second-unit offense at times. But those are the cards the Thunder have been dealt with. Their aspirations have been knocked down from title favorite to hopeful playoff team. But that shouldn't take away from his stepping up in this last month's worth of games.

Just a shame a lot of it is going in vain. Williams has been awesome. He's found a second wind in his NBA journey after settling in as a locker-room guy for the last couple of years. It will be interesting to see how much more he has left in the tank as OKC navigates through another month-plus of this current reality until Chet Holmgren arrives.

As the final seconds ticked away, Stirtz was leaving his first NBA trip to Miami with something. The 23-year-old drained an outside jumper to supersede his career high — which was set in the previous game. Silver linings, folks. That's what this hellish season has come down to.

Stirtz finished with 21 points on 7-of-14 shooting, five assists and three rebounds. He shot 5-of-12 from 3 and went 2-of-2 on free throws.

Entering the season, Stirtz didn't want to stand out for the wrong reasons. Instead, he fell in line seamlessly in OKC's established pecking order. No way you can take more shots than Gilgeous-Alexander and others, right? Well, that imaginary threshold wasn't a problem tonight. He let the ball rip from his hands. Which, funny enough, is exactly what the Thunder had hoped to see from him.

As soon as the ball was in his hands, Stirtz went up for a shot attempt. He reached double-digit outside attempts for the first time in his career. Out of necessity, too. That was one of the few avenues to the Thunder generating offense. Finally in rhythm, he caught fire with 11 points in the final frame. Sure, in garbage time, but that caveat is irrelevant for an NBA rookie trying to find his footing.

Expect the Thunder to rely on Stirtz more often. His playing time has been inconsistent through the first month. But with how dire their offense has deteriorated, they badly need secondary scoring and shot-making. Even if it's from a rookie who struggles on defense. The 23-year-old has grouped together his two best NBA games in the last couple of days. Let's see if he can add to the momentum.
